item.title: DOJ files hate crime charges against 22-year-old accused of plotting synagogue pipe bombing
item.dc:creator: Kaelan Deese
item.description: The Department of Justice on Thursday announced charges against a 22-year-old Utah man for attempting to commit a hate crime after he allegedly threatened online to blow up a synagogue and investigators found six improvised explosive pipe bombs at his home. Skyler AJ Rose of Ogden was indicted by a federal grand jury in Salt […]
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Justice on Thursday announced charges against a 22-year-old Utah man for attempting to commit a hate crime after he allegedly threatened online to blow up a synagogue and investigators found six improvised explosive pipe bombs at his home.

Skyler AJ Rose of Ogden was indicted by a federal grand jury in Salt Lake City the day before on charges including possession of an unregistered destructive device, threatening to kill or injure people and destroy a building with an explosive, and attempting to commit a hate crime, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah. Authorities also uncovered evidence containing child sexual abuse material, or CSAM, on his personal smartphone.

Images provided by the DOJ on Thursday show at least five alleged explosive devices with metal tubing located in a metal briefcase allegedly belonging to Rose, as well as a separate photo from a raid featuring one of the devices on top of a table with other precursor ingredients next to a white can of creatine.

Rose was arrested by local authorities last year as officials investigated the alleged antisemitic threats, according to the DOJ. He is scheduled to make his initial appearance in federal court Friday afternoon at the Orrin G. Hatch U.S. Courthouse in Salt Lake City. He has yet to enter a plea in the federal case.

The alleged threats were posted online in December 2025. One post said, “I want to blow up a synagogue,” prosecutors said. The FBI contacted the Ogden City Police Department because of the posts and assisted local officers in visiting Rose’s home.

Authorities later executed a search warrant and recovered the six improvised explosive pipe bombs, one inert device, explosive precursors, and components that could be used to build additional devices. They also found a black Samsung cellphone and two rifles with accompanying magazines and ammunition. The DOJ described the pipe bombs as functional.

A second warrant for Rose’s cellphone showed that he had searched online for a synagogue near him in November 2025, according to court documents. Investigators also found hundreds of cached images and screenshots containing evidence of CSAM.

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who traveled to Salt Lake City Thursday to announce the charges, said the indictment stopped “an alleged plan to carry out a violent attack on a synagogue.”

U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak said the charges should serve as a warning and a deterrent to anyone who attacks or attempts to attack a place of worship.

FBI Special Agent in Charge Robert Bohls said the bureau takes every threat seriously and credited the rapid collaboration among law enforcement agencies with helping protect lives from potential harm.

DOJ INVESTIGATES WHETHER COREY LEWANDOWSKI PROFITED FROM DHS ROLE

The case is being investigated jointly by the FBI and Ogden police, with assistance from the Utah Department of Public Safety, bomb squads from Davis and Weber counties, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Weber County Attorney’s Office.

If convicted on all five counts in the indictment, Rose could face a theoretical maximum of 70 years in prison, although the actual sentence would depend on the federal sentencing guidelines and whether the terms run concurrently or consecutively.

item.title: Supreme Court allows New Hampshire to bar student IDs for voting
item.dc:creator: David Zimmermann
item.description: The Supreme Court issued a ruling on Thursday, letting New Hampshire prohibit voters from using student identification cards to prove their identities before casting ballots in the midterm elections. The decision reverses a federal judge’s order blocking New Hampshire from enforcing a law that barred student IDs from being used for voter ID. The law […]
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling on Thursday, letting New Hampshire prohibit voters from using student identification cards to prove their identities before casting ballots in the midterm elections.

The decision reverses a federal judge’s order blocking New Hampshire from enforcing a law that barred student IDs from being used for voter ID. The law took effect in April and remained in place for the state’s primary elections in September until the judge put a block on the measure earlier this month.

The high court reasoned that U.S. District Judge Joseph Laplante, an appointee of former President George W. Bush, had no place to block the law 32 days before the general election.

“‘This Court has repeatedly emphasized that lower federal courts should ordinarily not alter the election rules on the eve of an election,'” the Supreme Court said in recapping a key point from a 2020 case before making its conclusion in the current case. “Here, the District Court did not point to anything that would justify deviating from that principle.”

The three-page order was unsigned, with Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson being the sole dissenter.

“I respectfully dissent because — even, and perhaps especially, when an election is looming — I would not disturb a clearly justifiable federal-court order issued to ensure that the public receives accurate information about a State’s electoral processes,” Jackson wrote.

New Hampshire Secretary of State David Scanlan, a Republican, filed the emergency petition with the Supreme Court after an appeals court declined to pause Laplante’s ruling. Scanlan had the support of the Republican National Committee in the case.

The state law banning student IDs from voting was challenged by the Coalition for Open Democracy, which argued the measure unlawfully burdened the right to vote and discriminated against young voters.

NEW HAMPSHIRE URGES SUPREME COURT TO REINSTATE STUDENT ID VOTING BAN AHEAD OF ELECTION

New Hampshire offers in-person voting on Election Day and mail-in voting, but it does not offer in-person early voting.

The state’s top race is the Senate election between Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH) and former New Hampshire Republican Sen. John Sununu. Both candidates are competing for the seat held by retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH). The highly competitive race, which could determine which party controls the Senate, leans in favor of Pappas.

item.title: New York City votes to end century-old horse-drawn carriage industry
item.dc:creator: David Zimmermann
item.description: The New York City Council has voted to end the Big Apple’s horse-drawn carriage industry, which has been around for more than 160 years. The legislation passed in a 40-7 vote on Thursday afternoon. Its approval came just over a week after New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani made a deal with City Council Speaker […]
item.content:encoded:
The New York City Council has voted to end the Big Apple’s horse-drawn carriage industry, which has been around for more than 160 years.

The legislation passed in a 40-7 vote on Thursday afternoon. Its approval came just over a week after New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani made a deal with City Council Speaker Julie Menin to ban horse-drawn carriages in less than two years.

The end result of that agreement was Romanch’s Law, which was named after an 18-year-old tourist, Romanch Mahajan, who died in June after falling from a carriage when the horse ran away. His death, which was the first and only human fatality connected to a horse-carriage accident, sparked action from local lawmakers.

The bill effectively bans all horse-drawn carriages in New York City, including Central Park, by June 1, 2028. It also prohibits the approval of new carriage licenses and ensures a transition plan is in place.

Such a plan would presumably include protections for carriage workers and the removal of carriage horses. The legislation stipulates that no horses will be slaughtered or transferred to another horse-drawn carriage business. Instead, the measure mandates the “humane disposition of carriage horses.”

Mamdani still needs to sign the bill, which is guaranteed to happen given his support for city officials and animal rights advocates pushing the ban.

The mayor said his administration is committed to making sure carriage workers are “protected” and the horses are “safe.”

Advocates were largely concerned about the safety of the horses, with about 40 horses dying on the job since 1982. But the livelihoods of carriage operators, many of whom are immigrants, will be harmed by the bill’s enactment.

The Transport Workers Union is already planning to sue New York City once Mamdani signs the bill into law. More lawsuits may be filed, New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino predicted before the vote took place.

“There will be a lawsuit coming up because this is unconstitutional,” the Republican lawmaker told Fox News. “Intro 943 is unconstitutional. Lawsuits are going to be filed immediately after this effort is passed. They’re going to be tangled up in legalese.”

Regardless of legal threats, the City Council’s top leader is taking the bill’s passage as a win.

“Today’s historic vote marks our commitment to animal welfare, public safety, and protecting workers,” Menin posted on X after the final vote. “Thank you to my colleagues, the advocates, and the countless New Yorkers who have worked for years to make this day possible.”

TRUMP DECRIES MAMDANI DEAL TO BAN NEW YORK CITY HORSE CARRIAGES: ‘SO SAD’

Hours before the City Council voted, President Donald Trump complained about the city ending its century-old horse-drawn carriage industry for “political reasons.”

“It was a Great Tradition,” he wrote in part on Truth Social. “Another piece of History that’s gone. It will be missed!”

item.title: Over 100 arrested in California after $2 billion state-federal healthcare fraud crackdowns
item.dc:creator: Kaelan Deese
item.description: Federal and California officials announced separate healthcare fraud crackdowns on Thursday, with federal prosecutors charging 15 people in cases alleging more than $2 billion in losses and state Attorney General Rob Bonta (D) announcing charges and arrests against 103 providers accused of defrauding Medi-Cal, the state’s version of Medicaid, of more than $4.5 million. Justice […]
item.content:encoded:
Federal and California officials announced separate healthcare fraud crackdowns on Thursday, with federal prosecutors charging 15 people in cases alleging more than $2 billion in losses and state Attorney General Rob Bonta (D) announcing charges and arrests against 103 providers accused of defrauding Medi-Cal, the state’s version of Medicaid, of more than $4.5 million.

Justice Department officials said at a press conference Thursday in Los Angeles that 10 of the 15 federal defendants were in custody, including eight arrested Thursday and two apprehended last week. The cases involve sham substance abuse treatment, unnecessary artery procedures, hospice services, genetic testing, and prescription drugs.

The largest case brought by the federal government alleged that Los Angeles father David Young, 71, and his son Nathan Young, 39, controlled dozens of substance abuse treatment companies and billed private insurers more than $1.6 billion for treatment that was medically unnecessary or never provided.

The Youngs allegedly used recruiters to bring vulnerable people, including homeless people and those struggling with addiction, to Southern California. Prosecutors said patients were promised free flights, housing, money, drugs, gift cards, and stays in luxury accommodations.

Some patients were allegedly kept addicted, cycled through treatment facilities, or placed in housing after their insurance benefits were exhausted. Officials said some were ultimately left on the streets of California.

“This is a pipeline of addicts and homeless people here to California,” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli, an appointee of President Donald Trump, said during a news conference. “Every dollar that’s defrauded by a fraudster is one less dollar that’s going to a patient who’s dying or has a disease or needs treatment.”

Federal prosecutors also charged cardiothoracic surgeon Harold Tabaie, 78, and chiropractor Hany Malek, 61, in a case involving about $135 million in allegedly fraudulent Medicare claims. Tabaie allegedly performed unnecessary atherectomies, invasive procedures used to remove plaque from arteries, on patients who did not need them. Malek allegedly posed as a medical doctor and recommended the surgeries.

Some patients allegedly underwent the procedure more than once after being told the first surgery had failed. Officials said patients were harmed during some of the operations.

Another case involved Dr. Richard Keech, 83, a physician and medical director for at least two hospices. Prosecutors alleged Keech signed certificates stating that Medicare patients were terminally ill even when they had not elected hospice care and were not expected to die within six months. The charges came as California hospice agencies faced heightened fraud scrutiny.

“Turning that benefit into a billing machine is about the most egregious theft from hardworking Americans that any of us can imagine,” Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald said.

Bonta’s competing fraud announcement on Thursday comes as the state’s Democratic attorney general is facing reelection early next month. His office announced felony charges against 103 In-Home Supportive Services providers accused of defrauding Medi-Cal of more than $4.5 million.

The providers involved in the state-level charges allegedly billed for care hours while patients were admitted to hospitals or skilled nursing facilities. The cases resulted from a statewide review involving data analysis, claims checks, and investigations across 17 counties.

House Republicans, including Reps. Brett Guthrie (R-KY), John Joyce (R-PA), Morgan Griffith (R-VA), and Jason Smith (R-MO), have spent the past year pressing federal watchdogs to investigate what they described as weak oversight of Medicare and Medicaid fraud in California under Bonta’s leadership.

Bonta said in a statement to X on Thursday afternoon that “while the alleged fraud represents a small fraction of California’s $30 billion IHSS budget, any abuse of Medi-Cal jeopardizes funding for our most vulnerable residents.”

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION WITHHOLDS $1.2 BILLION IN FEDERAL MEDICAID FUNDING FROM CALIFORNIA

The HHS inspector general conditionally recertified California’s Medicaid Fraud Control Unit in July, finding that it was not effectively carrying out some of its investigative and prosecutorial responsibilities. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz has also suggested California officials have not done enough to prevent fraud, with his agency deferring $867.5 million in federal Medicaid payments while reviewing high-risk claims in the state’s in-home care programs.

Bonta won the primary earlier this year with 56.6% of the vote, an 18-point lead over Republican challenger Mike Gates, ex-Huntington Beach city attorney and former Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Civil Rights Division of the DOJ under Trump.

item.title: Elissa Slotkin’s contemporary Bolshevism
item.dc:creator: Christopher Tremoglie
item.description: Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) gave a preview of the harsh totalitarianism looming over the country should Democrats win control of Congress in the midterm elections. It involved harassment, intimidation, and nearly everything short of death directed at political opponents, specifically those considering seeking work in the Trump administration. She openly admitted that she wanted applicants […]
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) gave a preview of the harsh totalitarianism looming over the country should Democrats win control of Congress in the midterm elections. It involved harassment, intimidation, and nearly everything short of death directed at political opponents, specifically those considering seeking work in the Trump administration. She openly admitted that she wanted applicants to fear the consequences of doing so, characterizing her threats as a deterrent.

Slotkin made the remarks during a live forum on Oct. 13 hosted by the Institute of Politics at the University of Chicago. The senator suggested that any young person seeking employment with the Trump administration could find themselves facing a dystopian exercise in guilt by association in what seem to be the inevitable show trials orchestrated by Democrats should they return to power after the election.

“I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration?” Slotkin said at the event. “Like, that sounds fun. I might get an opportunity.’ I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want, and so let me avoid participating in that.’ I want that deterrence message sent.”

THIS DEMOCRATIC CONGRESSWOMAN IS HOLDING ‘RESISTANCE LABS’ TO SUBVERT THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

She calls it a message of deterrence. In reality, it’s a warning of left-wing destruction. Slotkin’s comments were an act of intimidation and a threat, the kind regularly issued by bullies.

Slotkin’s words represented the kind of abuse of power and restrictions on liberties that the Founding Fathers warned about when they created this republic. Moreover, Slotkin’s words were particularly rich given her history of criticizing the president for allegedly abusing his political power. She was supposed to be a political beacon of morality, yet her words and threatening actions reveal that she is just as bad as the very people she claimed to abhor the most.

Slotkin’s comments more closely resembled the warnings issued by the Bolsheviks during the Russian Revolution in 1917 than those of a sitting U.S. senator in 2026. While she hasn’t called for political violence, sending dissenters to gulags, or executing political rivals, her calls for political intimidation are eerily similar to many of the nonviolent actions taken by the Bolsheviks in the Soviet Union. Her threats of legal ramifications and warnings that applicants for administration jobs could encounter “a ton of problems” in the future are reminiscent of the denunciation strategies, high-pressure psychological tactics, and propaganda campaigns the Bolsheviks used to eliminate dissent and opposition in the 1920s.

JOSH SHAPIRO TOO COWARDLY TO DENOUNCE BLACK MAN’S RACISM IN ALLEGED KILLING OF WHITE PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER

But should anyone be surprised by Slotkin’s flippant attitude and hints of intimidation? After all, she is a member of the political party that, during former President Joe Biden’s term in office, sought to silence President Donald Trump on social media platforms, ban social media accounts that challenged administration messaging on the efficacy of COVID-19 remedies, and work behind the scenes to suppress the voice of Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY). There was also the time when the Biden administration flirted with appointing Nina Jankowicz as a disinformation czar before retreating from that initiative.

All of these horrors and abuses of power are likely to return should Democrats win the 2026 midterm elections.

Maya Angelou famously said, “When someone shows you who they are, believe them the first time.” Slotkin has been showing Americans who she is since she was first elected to Congress in 2018. Democrats have been doing the same for over a decade, since Trump arrived on the political scene. No one should be surprised by their thirst for contemporary Bolshevism, and everyone should remember it as they cast their votes on Nov. 3.

item.title: Elon Musk backs David Ellison’s Skydance with $1 billion investment: Report
item.dc:creator: David Zimmermann
item.description: Elon Musk has reportedly invested $1 billion in Skydance, the media conglomerate that completed the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this month. The news comes after previous reporting indicating that Skydance CEO and Chairman David Ellison was asking Musk for a possible equity investment in his entertainment empire. The world’s richest […]
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk has reportedly invested $1 billion in Skydance, the media conglomerate that completed the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this month.

The news comes after previous reporting indicating that Skydance CEO and Chairman David Ellison was asking Musk for a possible equity investment in his entertainment empire.

The world’s richest man appears to have made such an investment, reported by Semafor and later confirmed by CNBC based on its own sources.

Musk has not commented on the investment himself, but he did congratulate Ellison on completing the merger days before it was expected to close.

Skydance’s chief executive is the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, who is an ally of President Donald Trump. The Ellison family’s connection to the president triggered critics’ concerns about Skydance’s control over CNN and CBS News.

Now that Musk is financially involved with Skydance, those concerns will likely be exacerbated even more.

There is speculation that Musk’s investment in Skydance is just the beginning, especially after media mogul John Malone predicted Musk would commit up to $10 billion to help pay down the media giant’s massive debt and possibly give SpaceX a stake in the entertainment business.

“I predict — big prediction — that you’ll see a global output deal for Skydance with SpaceX, and an investment by SpaceX into Skydance, to de-lever Skydance and take a little bit of the burden off David Ellison’s shoulders, because he’s taking on a pretty big pile of debt,” Malone said at an event earlier this week.

The newly combined company has nearly $80 billion in debt after closing the approximately $110 billion merger on Oct. 6. David Ellison and Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz have their work cut out for them in terms of meeting their $6 billion cost-savings goal to reduce the company’s burgeoning debt.

Larry Ellison is personally invested in Skydance, having put up more than $40 billion in equity financing and financial obligations to push the Paramount-Warner Bros. deal through to completion.

Because Larry Ellison is financially involved in Skydance, Malone makes the case that the Oracle executive will leverage his preexisting relationship with Musk to bring him on board.

“These guys are very intertwined,” Malone said. “Who helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it [for $44 billion in 2022]? Larry Ellison. OK, how did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long you’re going to see an announcement.”

WHAT’S NEXT FOR SKYDANCE AFTER PARAMOUNT-WARNER BROS. MERGER?

Indeed, reports of Musk’s investment came shortly after Malone made his prediction. There has been no announcement from Skydance about Musk’s involvement yet.

It remains to be seen if SpaceX, which owns and operates Starlink, will partner with Skydance in the near future.

item.title: Man accused of smashing Iwo Jima statue with sledgehammer in Quantico
item.dc:creator: Mackenzie Chase
item.description: A 27-year-old man named Miguel Alonso Maldonado Soriano was arrested Wednesday night after police said they caught him allegedly using a sledgehammer to destroy the Iwo Jima statue in Quantico, Virginia. Just before 10:15 p.m., officers responded to the area near Richmond Highway and Fuller Road to “investigate a destruction of property,” according to the […]
item.content:encoded:
A 27-year-old man named Miguel Alonso Maldonado Soriano was arrested Wednesday night after police said they caught him allegedly using a sledgehammer to destroy the Iwo Jima statue in Quantico, Virginia.

Just before 10:15 p.m., officers responded to the area near Richmond Highway and Fuller Road to “investigate a destruction of property,” according to the Prince William County Police Department. Upon arrival, police said they found a man using the sledgehammer to damage the statue, including decapitating a soldier.

Maldonado Soriano, from Stafford, Virginia, is facing charges of felony destruction of property, trespass with intent to damage property, and felony injury to a monument.

HOW CAN DEMOCRATS PROMOTE GUN CONTROL WHILE GOING SOFT ON GUN CRIMINALS?

Photos show the soldier’s head separated from the body. The cost of damage is estimated to be hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Maldonado Soriano is being held without bond, and his court date is pending.

item.title: DOJ investigates whether Corey Lewandowski profited from DHS role: Report
item.dc:creator: Molly Parks
item.description: The Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Corey Lewandowski, former adviser to fired Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, over allegations that he profited from his role at the department. The DOJ opened the criminal investigation into Lewandowski after a referral from the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general, according to multiple reports. Lewandowski is a […]
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Corey Lewandowski, former adviser to fired Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, over allegations that he profited from his role at the department.

The DOJ opened the criminal investigation into Lewandowski after a referral from the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general, according to multiple reports. Lewandowski is a longtime political ally of President Donald Trump, but he left the administration after Noem was fired in March.

Lewandowski denies wrongdoing, and his lawyer, Adam Trigg, rebuffed the DOJ inquiry in a statement to the New York Times.

“Mr. Lewandowski has not been contacted by the Justice Department regarding any investigation, and he denies any wrongdoing when he was proudly serving his country in a voluntary capacity,” Trigg said.

A source familiar with the matter confirmed that a referral was received by the DOJ and the department is investigating it. A spokesperson for the DOJ declined to comment.

The reports on the investigation did not include any specific details about the improper profiting allegations.

Lewandowski, a special government employee at DHS, served as Noem’s top adviser during her embattled tenure as department secretary. Lewandowski had a significant influence at the agency and played a role in directing the agency’s immigration operations.

In her final days as DHS secretary, Noem was grilled on Capitol Hill about DHS contracts worth $220 million for advertisements of her bolstering the agency’s self-deportation mechanism for illegal immigrants. Noem claimed during a Senate hearing that she had a “conversation” with Trump about the ads and was soon after fired by the president amid reports he was frustrated with her answers.

TRUMP SAYS DISHONEST PEOPLE HAVE TO BE PROSECUTED AFTER DOJ LAUNCHES AN INVESTIGATION INTO COREY LEWANDOWSKI

Noem also faced controversy in her final stretch in the job over her alleged affair with Lewandowski, though both deny any extramarital relationship.

Lewandowski and Noem also oversaw DHS when two U.S. citizens were killed by federal law enforcement during DHS immigration enforcement operations in Minneapolis.

Kaelan Deese contributed to this story.

item.title: Trump says dishonest people have to be prosecuted after DOJ launches investigation into Corey Lewandowski
item.dc:creator: Mabinty Quarshie
item.description: President Donald Trump declared that employees of his administration needed to be honest on the same day it was disclosed that the Department of Justice opened an inquiry into Corey Lewandowski, a former adviser at the Department of Homeland Security. The investigation reportedly originated from a referral from the DHS inspector general. It marks one […]
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump declared that employees of his administration needed to be honest on the same day it was disclosed that the Department of Justice opened an inquiry into Corey Lewandowski, a former adviser at the Department of Homeland Security.

The investigation reportedly originated from a referral from the DHS inspector general. It marks one of the rare instances of a Trump ally being investigated.

“All I know is I want my people to be honest, and if they’re not going to be honest, they have to be prosecuted,” Trump told reporters Thursday afternoon while speaking from the South Lawn.

“I don’t know about specifically, but because I view it, people are not honest. There’s stealing from me as president.”

Lewandowski’s close relationship with former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem sparked controversy as Noem was still married to her now-estranged husband. The two were pushed out of the department in March.

The DOJ is looking into whether Lewandowski, a Trump campaign manager in 2016, benefited from his role at DHS for personal financial gain, although his lawyer denied any wrongdoing. Lewandowski had extraordinary power as an adviser at DHS, including hosting meetings in Noem’s office without her presence.

DEMOCRATIC VIRGINIA STATE SEN. LOUISE LUCAS INDICTED IN ALLEGED MARIJUANA RACKETEERING SCHEME

The president claimed he didn’t know about the specifics of the investigation, but again stood firm on the importance of honesty in his administration in the wake of several allegations of corruption. Former Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned in the wake of allegations that she pressured a Trump donor to pay off her $100,000 American Express credit card debt.

“So I want my people to be honest,” Trump added. “And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do.”

item.title: 17-year-old arrested, accused of ISIS-backed assassination plot against Rep. Keith Self
item.dc:creator: Mackenzie Chase
item.description: The FBI has arrested a 17-year-old boy from McKinney, Texas, alleging that he was plotting an assassination against Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) on behalf of the Islamic State group. Self told the Washington Examiner he was notified of the plot by Capitol Police, who had been in communication with the FBI concerning comments the suspect […]
item.content:encoded:
The FBI has arrested a 17-year-old boy from McKinney, Texas, alleging that he was plotting an assassination against Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) on behalf of the Islamic State group.

Self told the Washington Examiner he was notified of the plot by Capitol Police, who had been in communication with the FBI concerning comments the suspect made. Self was later informed that he was the target of the attack set to take place on Oct. 17.

“I was in the military for 25 years, deployed several times, so, you know, I’m actually glad this happened to me and not one of my colleagues who has no experience like that because it tends to freak people out when you tell them that somebody’s trying to kill them,” Self said. “So, you know, it’s probably better to happen to me.”

Self posted on X expressing gratitude Wednesday to law enforcement and reaffirming his dedication to serving his constituents in Texas.

“I am grateful to the FBI and law enforcement for stopping this threat,” Self wrote. “My family and I are safe, and I remain focused on serving the people of Texas’ 3rd District.”

The teenager had been radicalized, and the attack is believed to have been motivated by ISIS, Self told the Washington Examiner.

Self is avidly against Islamic extremism and Sharia law. He is head of the Sharia-Free America Caucus alongside Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX), which was launched by the two lawmakers in 2025. At the time, Roy and Self said the move was necessary to “counter the alarming rise of Sharia Law in the United States. Sharia is a dominating force that is not compatible with the U.S. Constitution,” according to a Dec. 18, 2025, press release. Self said “the American way of life is under siege by radicals from a culture waging war against our Constitution and Western values.”

Self told the Washington Examiner he believed his efforts to push back against Sharia law and Islamic extremism were the reason he was targeted. In McKinney, Texas, Self said a recall vote was underway on the city council after a unanimous vote in August approved a site plan for a local mosque.

“So you know, you have to believe with all of the media attention on that city council vote, and I spoke at the city council, and I’ve been vocal as, you say, with the Sharia-Free America caucus, so yes, you have to believe that made me the target,” he said.

In his recent social media post, Self said he will “not back down” against “radical Islam.”

“Preserving our constitutional republic from radical Islam means accepting the costs that come with it—name-calling, threats, and worse,” he said. “Our Founders believed this country was worth the sacrifice. I served 25 years in the military because defending freedom was worth the sacrifice. This only strengthens my resolve. I will not back down.”

While representatives receive threats all the time, Self told the Washington Examiner that assassination plots don’t happen often.

“That’s what made this different,” Self said. “There was an actual arrest with the FBI saying that it was an assassination attempt. So that is unusual, yes. So, my response was frankly that we’ve simply got to be more vigilant.”

ABDUL EL SAYED, MIKE ROGERS CLASH OVER MAGA, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD IN FINAL MICHIGAN SENATE DEBATE

Self said his security team was prepared in case of any possible copycats, but has reaffirmed this plot didn’t shake his resolve.

“It will not deter me,” he said. “We will continue to work to defend the U.S. Constitution and our culture and this will not deter me in the least.”

The Washington Examiner reached out to the FBI for comment.
